To align the caption of a table to the left in LaTeX without using the `caption` package, you can use the `\captionof` command from the `caption` package (if allowed) or manually adjust the caption formatting. However, if you strictly cannot use the `caption` package, here are a few alternative approaches:

### 1. **Using `\caption` with `\raggedright`**
   You can redefine the `\@makecaption` command to left-align the caption. Add the following to your preamble:

   ```latex
   \makeatletter
   \long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
     \vskip\abovecaptionskip
     \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%
     \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
       #1: #2\par
     \else
       \global \@minipagefalse
       \hbox to\hsize{\raggedright #1: #2\hfil}%
     \fi
     \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
   \makeatother
   ```

   Then use `\caption` as usual:
   ```latex
   \begin{table}[h]
     \centering
     \begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
       \hline
       A & B \\
       \hline
       1 & 2 \\
       \hline
     \end{tabular}
     \caption{Left-aligned caption without the caption package.}
   \end{table}
   ```

### 2. **Using `\parbox` or `\minipage` for Manual Caption**
   If you don't want to redefine `\@makecaption`, you can manually place the caption inside a `\parbox` or `\minipage` with left alignment:

   ```latex
   \begin{table}[h]
     \centering
     \begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
       \hline
       A & B \\
       \hline
       1 & 2 \\
       \hline
     \end{tabular}
     \parbox{\linewidth}{\raggedright \captionof{table}{Left-aligned caption without the caption package.}}
   \end{table}
   ```

   (Note: This still uses `\captionof`, which is part of the `caption` package. If you cannot use it at all, proceed to the next method.)

### 3. **Manually Adding a Caption Without `\caption`**
   If you cannot use any caption-related commands, you can manually add a left-aligned label and description:

   ```latex
   \begin{table}[h]
     \centering
     \begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
       \hline
       A & B \\
       \hline
       1 & 2 \\
       \hline
     \end{tabular}
     \parbox{\linewidth}{\raggedright \textbf{Table 1:} Left-aligned caption without any caption package.}
   \end{table}
   ```

   (Note: You will need to manually manage table numbering if you use this approach.)

### 4. **Using `\multicolumn` for In-Table Caption**
   If you want the caption inside the table, you can use `\multicolumn`:

   ```latex
   \begin{table}[h]
     \centering
     \begin{tabular}{|l|}
       \hline
       \multicolumn{1}{|c|}{\textbf{Table 1: Left-aligned caption}} \\
       \hline
       A & B \\
       \hline
       1 & 2 \\
       \hline
     \end{tabular}
   \end{table}
   ```

### Best Approach Without `caption` Package
The first method (redefining `\@makecaption`) is the cleanest way to left-align captions without using the `caption` package. If you cannot modify internal LaTeX commands, the third method (manual caption) is the simplest alternative, though it requires manual numbering.
